package_info.why_malicious: The package contains heavily obfuscated JavaScript code that, when included in a web application, attaches event listeners to all forms in the DOM. Upon form submission, it serializes all user-entered data—including credentials—and silently exfiltrates it via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded, attacker-controlled domain. The package was distributed via typosquatting, leading to widespread credential and sensitive data theft from unsuspecting users.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the application is loaded in the browser)
execution_context.file_location: main JavaScript file of the package (e.g., index.js or dist/index.js)
required_permissions: DOM access (to read and manipulate forms)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code attaches submit event listeners to all forms in the DOM, serializes all form data upon each submission, and sends the serialized data via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain, resulting in silent exfiltration of user credentials and sensitive information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts every form submission on the page and exfiltrates all user-entered data—including credentials—to an external, attacker-controlled server. The use of obfuscation further indicates an attempt to conceal malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not intercept or exfiltrate sensitive user data such as credentials without explicit user consent. Normal analytics or telemetry libraries are transparent about data collection, avoid sensitive data, and allow opt-out.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some analytics or UX tools may collect non-sensitive form data (e.g., field completion rates) for improvement purposes, but they never collect credentials or do so without user awareness and consent.
key_indicators: Attaches submit event listeners to all forms in the DOM
Serializes complete form data, including credentials
Sends data via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded, non-affiliated external domain
Code is heavily obfuscated to hinder analysis
No user notification or consent for data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: A developer inadvertently installs the typosquatted malicious package 'icon-package' instead of the intended legitimate package.
attack_chain.leads_to: The malicious package is included in the developer's application or website, embedding its code in the production environment.

attack_chain.action: When the application or website is loaded in a user's browser, the malicious code executes in the browser context.
attack_chain.leads_to: The code attaches submit event listeners to all forms present in the DOM.

attack_chain.action: On every form submission, the code serializes all form data and sends it to the attacker's server via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of user credentials and other sensitive data to the attacker's infrastructure.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code that programmatically attaches submit event listeners to all forms in the DOM
Serialization of complete form data (including credentials) on submission
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to hardcoded, non-affiliated external domains from form submission handlers
Presence of obfuscated code that references external network destinations
file_indicators: index.js or dist/index.js containing obfuscated JavaScript code
References to document.querySelectorAll('form') and fetch or XMLHttpRequest calls to unknown domains
Hardcoded external URLs (e.g., https://attacker-domain.com/collect) in package source files
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to attacker-controlled domains not associated with the application vendor
Consistent use of the same external domain (e.g., attacker-domain.com/collect) across multiple package versions
Unusual POST traffic containing serialized form data from web applications using this package
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan JavaScript dependencies for code that attaches submit event listeners to all forms and serializes form data for network transmission. Flag packages containing obfuscated code with hardcoded external URLs. Monitor network traffic from web applications for unexpected POST requests to unknown or suspicious domains, especially those carrying serialized form data. Correlate findings with package installation sources to identify typosquatted or suspicious packages.
